text:
maria: Quick thread — I finished the offline replay A/B harness comparing two queue/prefetch policies + a small kernel selector tweak. TL;DR: prefetch-hysteresis wins tail on convo-heavy traces (~15% p99 improvement) but regresses median on short single-turn traffic (~6% median increase). CSV + traces uploaded to /mnt/sim/output/1957654321.zip :link: 

maria: Repro command I used: 
```
./simulator --replay-dir=/traces/weekly/ --policy=prefetch-hysteresis --kernel-bias=small-seq-prefer --token-budget=1024 --out=/mnt/sim/output/1957654321.csv
```

maria: Key config bits: `kv_prefetch=true`, `prefetch_hysteresis_ms=30`, `batch_formation=continuous`, `queue_window_ms=12` — we sweep hysteresis in {0,10,30,50} and token_budget in {512,1024,2048}.

anil: nice. how many sampled traces and what mix? 

maria: 4 traces: two large conv datasets (~1.2M requests), one short-queries trace (~400k), one mixed-webhook trace (~300k). overall ~3.2M requests. all runs seeded and replayer deterministic.

jordan: curious about the kernel selector interaction — you said you nudged it to prefer small-seq kernels. what exactly changed? :thinking: 

maria: yeah small change: when avg_sequence <= 32 we bias towards small-seq kernel path (lower mem, faster per-token for short sequences). it reduced per-token for short samples but when combined with hysteresis we saw increased median because hysteresis delays prefetch so some short requests didn't get KV warmed.

sam: can you paste the tiny patch? might help reason about race with batching. 

maria: patch snippet: 
```diff
- if (seq_len <= 32) kernel = default;
+ if (seq_len <= 32) kernel = small_seq_fast; // prefer low-latency path
```

lee: my hypothesis: hysteresis window + continuous batching means short requests often finish before their prefetch fires, so they miss warm KV but still incur overhead of waiting for batching decisions. suggests adaptive hysteresis per-route.

anil: agreed. also check token_budget interactions — with 1024 we got larger batches that mask kernel gains but make p50 worse for short queries.

perf-bot: Auto-report: A/B summary (1957654321) — conv-trace-A: p99 down 15% (hysteresis), p50 +3%; short-trace-B: p50 +6% (hysteresis), p99 unchanged. overall cost-per-token -2.1% for conv but +0.8% for short. Full CSV: /mnt/sim/output/1957654321_summary.csv

jordan: interesting. Can we run a follow-up: adaptive hysteresis where window = clamp( base_ms * sqrt(avg_seq_len/32), 0, 60 )? should bias low for short sequences.

maria: I can queue that. also want to try kernel-bias rollback + per-route token_budget tuning (lower token_budget for api-short route).

sam: +1. also run a warmup pass (pre-warm KV cache) before measuring median for short traces — add a `--kv-warmup=true` run to separate cold-hit effects.

lee: action items?

maria: action items: 1) run adaptive-hysteresis sweep (me, today) 2) run kernel-bias off + token_budget per-route (sam + jordan to coordinate) 3) kv-warmup baseline run (lee) 4) surface results to perf-dashboard and decide rollout canary config (anil). I'll post updated CSVs here. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

anil: thanks — ping me once the adaptive run finishes.

perf-bot: Scheduled job: adaptive-hysteresis-sweep queued (job id 1957654321-2). ETA 2h.

maria: great, thanks everyone. I'll post quick notes and the new CSV once available. :thumbsup:
